location.line_range: 1253-1260 (SocketBodyStream.close), 587 (retry closeQuietly(socket)); ProxyExchange.java 187-191 (release closes the attached SSLSocket)

findings.description: Cross-wave interaction of the TLS wave (SEC-PROXY-005: the attached socket is the SSLSocket) with the relay/lifetime waves (FR-PROXY-020, REL-PROXY-001) and the error path. Every normal end of an https exchange closes the SSLSocket itself: RelayedBodyStream.close -> SocketBodyStream.close -> BufferedInputStream.close -> SSLSocket AppInputStream.close -> SSLSocketImpl.close(), and ProxyExchange.release() -> closeQuietly(socket) on the error path. On the JDK (17 checked: SSLSocketImpl.duplexCloseOutput -> bruteForceCloseInput(hasCloseReceipt=false for TLS 1.3) -> appInput.deplete() -> SSLSocketInputRecord.deplete(tryToRead = SO_TIMEOUT > 0) -> is.read()) a TLS 1.3 duplex close sends close_notify and then blocks reading the plain socket for up to SO_TIMEOUT, which the proxy set to readTimeout. So against an https backend that keeps the connection open after its response (the FR-PROXY-020 AC-4 case), each request holds the worker thread and its maxConcurrent slot for one extra readTimeout (60 s by default) after the body was delivered; the InMemory adapter completes the client response only after that; HEAD/204/304 responses (closed at once) are hit the same way. On the error path (READ_TIMEOUT, INVALID_RESPONSE, CONNECT/TLS done but backend silent) forward()'s finally release() closes the SSLSocket and waits another readTimeout before the 504/502 reaches the error flow (2x readTimeout measured). The 502/503 retry path closeQuietly(socket) on an SSLSocket does the same before the retry wait, after retryAllowed() already checked that the wait fits the total deadline. TlsConnector/BackendClient.secure and the deadlines already avoid this by closing the plain socket; the release and body-close paths do not. TLS 1.2 is not affected (contrast test passes), so this shows with every JDK 11+ / modern backend default.
findings.suggested_fix: Never close the SSLSocket itself on the proxy's paths: keep the plain socket in ProxyExchange (already recorded as `plain`) and have release() close the plain socket (or both, plain first), and make SocketBodyStream.close() close the plain socket instead of the stream/SSLSocket (the connection is not reused, so no close_notify exchange is needed); likewise use the plain socket in the 502/503 retry close. Add an https variant of FR-PROXY-020 AC-4 and FR-PROXY-017 AC-4 to ProxyTlsTest/ProxyBackendConnectionTest.
findings.family: TLS 1.3 SSLSocket duplex close waits SO_TIMEOUT

evidence.intent_output: FR-PROXY-008 AC-3 (22.reverse-proxy.srs.md:1018): a chunked body that passes the limit while being forwarded makes the proxy close the backend connection. So opening a connection is expected for a chunked overrun.

findings.drop_reason: The proxy does open a TCP connection, but it sends 0 bytes on it. That matches the test's assertion message ('the backend saw no request') and is what the spec allows (FR-PROXY-008 AC-3). Only the test name 'WithoutReachingTheBackend' overstates. RawBackend.requestCount() counts only requests whose body ended, so it could also miss a partly sent request, but no such case was shown here.
findings.title: chunkedClientBodyOverTheRawLimitGives413WithoutReachingTheBackend: a backend connection is opened
findings.description: With rawBodyLimit(8) and a chunked 64-byte body, the proxy connects to the backend and then closes the connection without sending a byte. RawBackend.requestCount() stays 0 because it counts only requests whose head and body were read to the end.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: name the test '...WithoutSendingARequest', or count accepted connections if 'no connection' is what is meant.

clean_code.description: ResponseHeaderCopier.connectionNames re-implements HeaderRules.connectionNames (HeaderRules.java:122-136) with a slightly different element rule (non-token elements kept here, dropped there); one shared helper would keep request and response Connection handling consistent.

IPv4/IPv6 literal parsing exists three times: TargetUrl.isIpv4/isIpv6/countGroups, BackendRequest.isIpv4/isIpv6/groups (BackendRequest.java:141-220) and CertificateHostnames.ipv4/ipv6 (CertificateHostnames.java:156-263); hex-digit helpers are likewise repeated in PathChecker, CertificateHostnames and ChunkedBodyInputStream. Divergence between them (e.g. which literals TargetUrl accepts vs which CertificateHostnames can match) is a latent risk.

ResponseHeaderCopier.copy(List, Response), copy(List, Set, Response) and LocationRewriter.apply(List, TargetUrl, String, Response) (LocationRewriter.java:39-43) are called only from tests; production uses the PendingResponseHeaders variants.

Proxy.java (1262 lines) holds the public option API, the 15-argument Options copy constructors (one withX per option, order-sensitive same-type arguments), request-framing decisions, the retry loop, response header assembly and socket stream wrappers; the retry/attempt loop and the framing decision could live in their own package-private classes.

The FR-APP-027 status classification (HttpException status, 413 for an unwrapped BodyTooLargeException, else fallback) is re-implemented twice in Auth (routerError and prodAnswer) beside StandardErrors.statusOr (StandardErrors.java:33-39). A future classification change must be made in three places; expose one public/shared classifier instead.

The raw body limit default is initialised in three classes from JsonBodyReader.DEFAULT_LIMIT, and the generic LimitedInputStream.byteLimit range check reads JsonBodyReader.MAX_LIMIT: the raw/form/JSON limits are coupled to the JSON reader's constants. A shared BodyLimits constant holder would remove the duplication and the JSON-specific dependency.

DefaultRequest (897 lines) gained the raw body reader (rawStream + RawBodyStream), the header enumeration (HeaderEnumeration, headerKey, sameHeaderName) and proxy-trust exposure on top of JSON/form/cookie/query/upload handling. RawBodyStream and HeaderEnumeration are self-contained and could live in their own package-private classes as DeclaredLength already does.

The javadoc onlyIf guard exists for 'NaruServe-proxy before its first class' (package-info.java only). The proxy module now has 20 classes, so the guard is a stale wave-local workaround that silently publishes an empty javadoc jar if a module's sources ever regress to package-info only.
After isFieldValue moved to HttpHeaderValues, DefaultResponse keeps one-line delegators isToken/isFieldValue; callers could call HttpHeaderValues directly.

awaitConnections is copied word for word in ProxyExchangeTest:190 and ProxyLifetimeSocketTest:203. awaitCounterZero is in ProxyConcurrencyTest:226, ProxyLifetimeSocketTest:188 and ProxyTimeoutsTest:605. Raw-socket readHead/readFully/readLine helpers are reimplemented in RawBackend:163/220, ProxyErrorsTest:531/546, ProxyExchangeTest:780/805, ProxyLifetimeSocketTest:229/244, ProxyRequestHeadersTest:404, ProxyRequestBodyTest:574/587, ProxyTimeoutsTest:644/659 and ProxyBackendConnectionTest:399. One package-private test utility (for example next to RawBackend) would remove about ten copies.

RecordingBackend copies the accept/record/answer loop of NaruServe-proxy's RawBackend because test classes are not shared between modules. A testFixtures source set in NaruServe-proxy, like the one NaruServe-api already has, would let the servlet test reuse it.
